title: 3D-TokSIM: Stacking 3D Memory with Token-Stationary Compute-in-Memory for Speculative LLM Inference
problem: LLM autoregressive decoding faces severe memory bandwidth bottleneck from the logic die; 2D memory solutions cannot overcome this due to limited memory-to-logic bandwidth.
motivation: Speculative decoding reduces latency but intensifies memory bandwidth demands; vertical stacking with tight memory-compute coupling is necessary.
method: The architecture stacks 3D memory directly on the logic chip and uses compute-in-memory (doing computations where the data sits) to minimize shuttling data around. Instead of moving token data across the chip, it keeps tokens in place and brings computation to them, reducing data movement and power consumption. This approach optimizes resource allocation for more parallel token predictions during LLM decoding, accelerating the process.
key_novelty: Token-stationary compute-in-memory with 3D memory stacking (keeping tokens in place while computation moves to them) to overcome the memory bottleneck in LLM speculative decoding.
contributions: Token-stationary compute-in-memory architecture reducing intra-die data movement
3D memory stacking approach for improved memory bandwidth to logic
15.1x throughput and 324x energy efficiency improvements on Llama2-7B speculative decoding vs RTX 3090
limitations: Not discussed—focuses on architecture design without discussing scalability to larger models or different decoding strategies.
primary_theme: Token-stationary CIM with 3D memory for LLM speculative decoding
